Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

the meeting agenda includes the key list the inventory the hook labels and the recycling trial but the committee has not decided whether to add a separate discussion about the flickering light the caretaker will bring the original shed plan and Leon will bring the removable labels the notice is meant to give residents practical information rather than announce a final decision about any of the repairs people can write comments on the clipboard by the door until friday evening and the caretaker will take it to the housing office on monday morning after checking that no page has come loose", "output": "The bicycle shed behind Alder Court serves twelve flats and the small repair room beside the laundry, and people use it at different hours, so the notice board has to work for residents who leave before sunrise as well as those who come home late. The shed is narrow, but it holds fourteen bicycles if the front aisle stays clear and nobody leaves a trailer beside the emergency door. The east wall has six numbered hooks, and the west wall has a wooden rack that was installed by the housing cooperative in April. The floor slopes slightly toward the drain, and rainwater sometimes follows the rear wheel of a bicycle inside.

Last month, the caretaker moved the old pump and the red toolbox onto a shelf because they were blocking the aisle. The pump is still available, but its handle is loose, and the toolbox belongs to the repair group, not to any one resident. A short inventory on the board lists the pump, the toolbox, two tire levers, a patch kit, and a small hand brush. The spare chain is not in the box, even though an earlier note said it was there. Nobody has confirmed where it went, and the repair group plans to check the locked cupboard next Tuesday. The cupboard key is kept in the office and should be returned before closing.

Section one: The door and the key. The outer door sticks when the temperature drops and should be pulled firmly until the latch catches. Residents should not leave it propped open while they unload groceries because the shed opens directly onto the public path. A brass key is available from the housing office during weekday hours, and a second key is kept in a sealed envelope for the evening caretaker to use if the lock jams. The current key list is on the inside of the office cabinet, and it shows which flats have borrowed a key. The list does not say that every flat has one.

The committee asked me to send the revised shed notice to Nadia, not Otis, before the next building meeting because Nadia is preparing the welcome packet and Otis is only gathering estimates for the roof repair. The notice should say that bicycles must be secured to a hook or rack and that the aisle needs to remain open. It should also mention that residents can report a broken light to the caretaker without implying that the light has already been fixed. The light near the rear drain flickers every few minutes, and the electrician has not yet inspected it.

When I asked the caretaker about the small blue bicycle under the window, she said it had been left there by a visitor on Sunday afternoon and that she had moved it away from the drain. The bicycle has a paper tag with the number thirty-four, but the tag is damp and the writing is hard to read. The caretaker said there was no name on it, and she had not decided whether to move it to the office or wait for the owner to return. She asked that nobody lock it to the wooden rack in the meantime because its rear wheel is bent and could damage the lower rail.

A resident named Leon has offered to repaint the faded numbers on the east wall, but he wants to use removable labels first so the committee can check that the numbering matches the updated floor plan. The current hooks run from one through six, but hook four is partly hidden behind a rain jacket, and hook six has a loose screw. Leon can bring a screwdriver on Saturday if someone can open the shed for him. The caretaker is available after ten, but not between noon and one because she collects the mail from the central office.

The roof estimate is a separate matter and should not be added to the shed notice. The roofer measured the gutter above the repair room and said that leaves have gathered near the downpipe, but he has not given a price yet. Otis is comparing that estimate with a second one from a local contractor and expects to have both figures for the meeting. The roof work may need to wait until the cooperative approves its autumn budget, and nobody has said that the repair is scheduled. The repair room can still be used while the estimate is pending, as long as the folding table stays against the south wall.

On Thursday evening, the residents can test a new arrangement for the recycling crates outside the shed. The crates should stand along the brick wall rather than beside the entrance, so people carrying bicycles have room to turn. The trial will last for two weeks, and the caretaker will note whether collection staff can reach the lids. The glass crate is already cracked at one corner and should not be lifted by its rim. The collection company has been told about the crack but has not said when a replacement will arrive. Residents can put clean jars in the crate until then if they lower them carefully.

The meeting agenda includes the key list, the inventory, the hook labels, and the recycling trial, but the committee has not decided whether to add a separate discussion about the flickering light. The caretaker will bring the original shed plan, and Leon will bring the removable labels. The notice is meant to give residents practical information rather than announce a final decision about any of the repairs. People can write comments on the clipboard by the door until Friday evening, and the caretaker will take it to the housing office on Monday morning after checking that no page has come loose."}]
